examples.japanese: おたまで{味噌汁|みそしる}をよそった。
examples.english: I served miso soup with a ladle.

examples.japanese: このおたまは{深|ふか}くて{使|つか}いやすい。
examples.english: This ladle is deep and easy to use.

examples.japanese: おたまを{使|つか}って、スープを{鍋|なべ}から{器|うつわ}に{移|うつ}した。
examples.english: I used a ladle to transfer soup from the pot to the bowl.

examples.japanese: カレーを{作|つく}るときは、{大|おお}きいおたまがあると{便利|べんり}だ。
examples.english: When making curry, having a large ladle is convenient.

examples.japanese: おたまで{鍋|なべ}の{底|そこ}からよくかき{混|ま}ぜないと、{焦|こ}げてしまう。
examples.english: If you don't stir well from the bottom of the pot with a ladle, it will burn.

notes:
おたま is the common everyday word for a ladle used to serve soup, stew, and other liquid dishes. The full formal name is お{玉杓子|たまじゃくし}, shortened to おたま in daily use.

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- おたまでよそう (to serve/dish out with a ladle)
- おたまで{掬|すく}う (to scoop with a ladle)
- おたまでかき{混|ま}ぜる (to stir with a ladle)

ETYMOLOGY:
おたまじゃくし also means 'tadpole' because of the similar shape — a round head on a long handle. The kitchen utensil likely got its name from this resemblance.

RELATED KITCHEN UTENSILS:
- しゃもじ: rice paddle/scoop
- フライ{返|がえ}し: spatula
- {菜箸|さいばし}: cooking chopsticks
